t: Minimum Operations to Form Subsequence With Target Sum — Bit Greedy
o: Every element is a power of two; one operation splits 2^b into two 2^(b−1). Count how many of each power we hold. Scan target bits from LSB up, carrying surplus halves upward. When a needed bit is missing, break the nearest available higher power: that costs (higher − needed) operations and showers the lower bits with surplus pieces. Example 1: target 7 = 111; bits 0,1 exist, bit 2 requires splitting 8 → 1 op. Example 3: total sum 34 < 35 → −1.
k: Greedy LSB-to-MSB with surplus carrying; breaking the nearest higher power is locally optimal.

a.i: Keep cnt[b] = number of 2^b available. For each target bit, use one if present; otherwise find the lowest set bit above, pay the distance, and deposit two copies at each intermediate level, consuming one at the target level. Leftover pairs at level b promote to level b+1.
s: For b = 0..31: if target bit b set — use cnt[b] if nonzero, else locate the next higher nonempty cnt[j], add j−b to the answer, and cascade halves down, consuming one.
If no higher power exists, return −1.
Otherwise carry cnt[b] // 2 upward to cnt[b+1].
a.t: O(n + 32²) — bucketing plus the nested bit sweep (inner search bounded by 32)

w: Feasibility check first: if Σnums < target it's −1 immediately. Pitfalls: off-by-one in bit_length (2^b ↔ index b), remembering to consume the piece after cascading, and promoting surplus pairs each iteration. Follow-up: report WHICH operations to perform.
